title: SLO-driven alert tuning, automated runbooks, and circuit-breaker load-shedding playbook
creator: Amelia Rivera
description: Goal: Reduce alert noise while ensuring rapid wake-the-person coverage for true SLO burn / multi-region failover conditions. Deliver a codified runbook and automation that: (1) uses SLO windows and burn rates to drive progressive paging tiers, (2) integrates circuit-breaker + load-shedding triggers for in-flight traffic, and (3) provides automated mitigation playbooks that can be exercised in staging and triggered in prod with safe rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Alerts fire only for SLO burn > 5% over 5m or region outage detected by heartbeat voting; 2) PagerDuty routes progressive paging: SE on-call -> infra SRE -> CTO escalation only after 30m unresolved critical incident; 3) Automated runbook executes safe rate-limit ramp and model-fallback with a single button or API trigger; 4) Runbook contains explicit multi-region failover steps and circuit-breaker reset guidance; 5) Test drills run in staging with < 1hr runbook execution time and postmortem checklist.
decisions: - Primary alert thresholds will be SLO-burn-rate focused rather than raw error rate; - Use voting across region heartbeats to avoid noisy single-region flaps; - Circuit breaker decisions live in the edge proxy (Envoy) with a secondary check in the runtime to stop token generation when backpressure is detected; - Runbook automation will be implemented as GitHub Actions workflows with feature flags for manual/auto modes.
tradeoffs:
- Raising thresholds reduces wakeups but increases time-to-detect for some degradations; mitigated by progressive paging and synthetic canary checks.
- Automating rollback of model-fallback reduces human error but risks cascading churn if the fallback has a latent bug; we add canary gating and post-rollback validation.
- Moving circuit-breaker logic to proxies reduces load on runtime but complicates coordination across regions; adding a lightweight KV sync for breaker state is chosen to keep decisions fast.

planned_automation:
- GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/auto-mitigation.yml (triggers: PD webhook, manual button, scheduled drills)
- Lambda/Cloud Function to execute safe rate-limit increases and model-fallback API calls with automatic validations
- Grafana Alertmanager configuration to translate SLO burn into structured PD alerts with context and runbook link
- Runbook test suite (playback of 10 failure modes) that runs nightly in staging
runbook_excerpt:
1) Detect: Confirm SLO burn > 5% over 5m OR majority heartbeat fail across regions.
2) Contain: Enable proxy circuit-breaker in target region (cmd: rdxctl proxy cb enable region-<x>) and enable runtime KV cache bypass.
3) Mitigate: Trigger model-fallback to quantized-variant (API: POST /admin/fallback?model=redwood-q2b) and increase rate-limit throttle to 60% for non-critical tenants.
4) Validate: Run the smoke-checks dashboard: /dashboards/smoke-slo and verify 50% reduction in tail-latency within 3m.
5) Escalate: If unresolved after 20m, page Infra SRE. After 60m, run multi-region failover checklist.
6) Recover: Gradually restore normal rates and disable circuit-breaker once 10m of healthy metrics are observed.
